answer: Each identity registers a beacon emitting a plume signal with a saffron tag at one site, and reef sensors record its origin, fingerprint, and saffron tag; auditors recheck randomly, and a missing, duplicated, or mislocated signal burns an 80-credit bond. The k-th beacon by the same payer costs 120+20(k-1) credits as site fees rise, so 1,000 fakes cost 10,110,000 credits. A rented beacon farm fails: beacons in one warehouse share one origin and fingerprint, so sensors flag the cluster and burn them. An honest agent registers one beacon, pays 120 once, and recovers 80 after one clean epoch.
